He played [[college basketball]] for the [[Baylor Bears men's basketball|Baylor Bears]]. He was a consensus five-star [[college recruiting|recruit]] and one of the top players in the 2023 class. ==Early life and high school career== Walter grew up in [[McKinney, Texas]] and initially attended [[McKinney High School]].{{cite web|url=https://www.si.com/college/texas/mens-basketball/longhorns-jakobe-walter-visit-austin-chris-beard-commitment-recruit-dillon-mitchell-arterio-morris|title=Elite In-State SG Ja’Kobe Walter Visiting Texas this Weekend|first=Zach|last=Dimmitt|website=[[SI.com]]|date=April 30, 2022|access-date=February 24, 2023}} A [[shooting guard]], he averaged 23.3 points, 7.6 rebounds, 1.9 assists, and 2.3 steals per game as a junior as McKinney won the state championship.{{cite web|url=https://theathletic.com/4175007/2022/06/22/baylor-lands-5-star-shooting-guard-jakobe-walter/|title=Baylor lands 5-star shooting guard Ja’Kobe Walter|website=[[The Athletic]]|date=June 21, 2022|access-date=February 24, 2023}} Walter transferred to [[Link Academy (Missouri)|Link Academy]] in [[Branson, Missouri]] prior to the start of his senior year.{{cite web |last=McFarland |first=Shawn |date=May 5, 2022 |title=McKinney five-star junior Ja’Kobe Walter will play final season at Link Academy (Mo.) |work=[[Dallas Morning News]]}} Walter was selected to play in the [[2023 McDonald's All-American Boys Game]] during his senior year.{{cite web|url=https://wacotrib.com/sports/college/baylor/baylor-signee-walter-named-mcdonalds-all-american/article_8b19a6a2-9c40-11ed-a78b-1fbc6cc3334d.html|title=Baylor signee Walter named McDonald's
